pages.heading: August 2025: Witkoff mission, CPB defunding, and the BLS firing
pages.body: Trump confirmed in early August 2025 that special envoy Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow within days, ahead of the expiry of a 10-day ultimatum for Russia to reach a peace agreement with Ukraine, saying the goal was to "get a deal where people stop getting killed" while conceding Russians were "wily characters" adept at avoiding sanctions.[n] In May 2025 he signed an executive order directing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting to cease federal funding for PBS and NPR, a step that with congressional rescissions led the CPB to announce its wind-down in August.[n] On August 1, 2025 he ordered the dismissal of Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner Erika McEntarfer after a weak July jobs report with large downward revisions, calling the numbers "faked" and promising a more "competent and qualified" replacement.[n] The same period saw the Office of Special Counsel open a Hatch Act review of former special counsel Jack Smith over his prosecutions of Trump, and the Justice Department file a misconduct complaint against Chief Judge James Boasberg.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 silence on the Witkoff Gaza report
pages.body: Badlands commentary argued that the White House's failure to publicize Steve Witkoff's findings after his visit to Gaza aid sites suggested it was "circling the wagons and wargaming the next move" rather than exonerating Israel of starvation and war-crime allegations.[n] The White House had also requested, and the House approved in June 2025, a $1.1 billion clawback of appropriated Corporation for Public Broadcasting funds.[n]

pages.heading: 2025 elimination of public broadcasting funding
pages.body: Congress eliminated federal funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting in 2025, with the House approving a White House request to claw back $1.1 billion in already appropriated funds in June and the Senate Appropriations Committee's 2026 bill zeroing out CPB funding for the first time in over 50 years.[n]

pages.heading: 2025 misconduct complaint against Judge Boasberg
pages.body: At Attorney General Pam Bondi's direction, the Justice Department filed a misconduct complaint in July 2025 against U.S. District Court Chief Judge James Boasberg over public remarks that the Trump administration would disregard federal court rulings and cause a constitutional crisis.[n] Department officials said the comments violated the Code of Conduct for United States Judges and eroded confidence in judicial neutrality.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 Gaza allegations
pages.body: Badlands commentary in August 2025 referenced widespread allegations of starvation and other war crimes against the IDF in Gaza, arguing the Trump administration's silence after envoy Steve Witkoff's aid-site visit implied those claims had been substantiated rather than refuted.[n] Israeli fire killed 18 people in Gaza during the same period in which Hamas restated its refusal to disarm.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 commentary
pages.body: Ashe in America argued that defenders of public broadcasting invoked rural weather and emergency alerts to obscure their real fear — that defunding would expose the absence of a market for what she called global communist propaganda.[n] She also framed the Texas antitrust case against BlackRock, State Street and Vanguard as vindication of long-derided claims about asset managers driving social change, and warned that reports of ChatGPT giving Molech ritual and self-harm instructions would be dismissed as a second Satanic panic.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 commentary
pages.body: Herold called the declassified whistleblower testimony on the Trump–Russia intelligence assessment one of the most damning disclosures to date and urged DNI Tulsi Gabbard to un-redact the name of the official who shut the whistleblower down and to declassify Enclosure 3.[n] Commenting on the Office of Special Counsel's review of Jack Smith, he invoked Justice Clarence Thomas's immunity concurrence and its line that "a private citizen cannot criminally prosecute anyone, let alone a former President."[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 commentary
pages.body: GhostofBasedPatrickHenry speculated that Steve Witkoff's silence after inspecting Gaza aid sites, and his abrupt cancellation of a Moscow trip, indicated he had confirmed allegations against Israel, and suggested Syria and Palestine could enter negotiations with Russia.[n] He also mocked the UN's study finding its own reports go unread and credited Kim Jong Un's balloon campaign with baiting South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol into the martial law gambit that ended his presidency.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 commentary on Hamas
pages.body: Chris Paul argued that the arc from the October 7 attack through eventual confirmation of a Palestinian state and the end of "Hamas" constitutes a long, divisive narrative cycle acclimating the world to a post-2020 "new normal," and contended that a Palestinian state already exists and that terrorist groups function as private armies of a global regime, like the cartels.[n]

pages.heading: August 2025 projects
pages.body: Badlands Media promoted the premiere of CODEX 911, an original film by contributor Brad Zerbo, at GART Deadwood with virtual ticketing, and its Burning Bright Publishing imprint's debut novel Saving Seoul.[n]
